description: A chief commercial counsel must decide whether to approve a customer-support AI platform agreement and finalize the data-use, security, insurance, and audit protections, with input from privacy counsel, insurance counsel, and customer contracts counsel.

shared_context.S1: The company plans to use the vendor's AI platform to handle customer-support chats and call transcripts beginning next quarter.
shared_context.S2: The vendor has provided a draft agreement for review, including its standard data-use, liability, insurance, and audit provisions.
shared_context.S3: Elena Marquez gives final approval before the company signs.
shared_context.S4: The contract-approval workflow includes a scheduled round in which privacy, insurance, and customer-contracts counsel each state their findings in turn before final approval. Each counsel is expected to give the substantive findings immediately when called, without a preliminary acknowledgment or discussion. After the third counsel completes the findings round, Elena records the approval decision immediately rather than opening another discussion round.

PF1.text: While reviewing the proposed data flows against the company's privacy inventory, Daniel confirmed that the platform will process identifiable customer call transcripts. The company's approved data-processing standard therefore requires deletion within exactly 7 calendar days after termination, prohibits use of customer content for model training, prohibits use for service improvement, and requires processing exclusively in the European Union; these points have not yet been entered in the contract redline.

PF2.text: Maya confirmed with the company's insurance broker that the cyber policy covers this deployment only if the vendor maintains at least $5,000,000 of cyber-liability insurance and names the company as an additional insured. She received the broker's written confirmation yesterday but has not added it to the approval checklist.

PF3.text: Thomas reviewed the enterprise customer's existing master agreement and confirmed that the company may use an AI subcontractor for support only if the subcontractor grants an annual audit right and accepts uncapped indemnity for both confidentiality breaches and personal-data breaches. He has not yet incorporated those flow-down requirements into the vendor agreement.

acceptance_conditions: Customer content must be deleted exactly 7 calendar days after termination.
The vendor must be prohibited from using customer content for model training.
The vendor must be prohibited from using customer content for service improvement.
Processing must be restricted to the European Union.
The vendor must maintain at least $5,000,000 of cyber-liability insurance.
The company must be named as an additional insured.
The broker confirmation must be recorded as received.
The agreement must grant an annual audit right.

decisive_facts.why: The approved privacy standard changes the settlement to exactly 7 days of deletion, prohibits both model-training and service-improvement use, and restricts processing to the European Union.
The broker's coverage condition changes the settlement to at least $5,000,000 of vendor cyber insurance, company additional-insured status, and a recorded broker confirmation.
The enterprise customer's flow-down terms change the settlement to an annual audit right and separate uncapped indemnity requirements for confidentiality breaches and personal-data breaches.
